entries.clue: Taking part in frottage is terribly unkind to the elderly (6)

indicatorNotes.Taking part in: Taking part in something is taking a piece of what is already inside it, so only a run of letters within the words that follow is wanted.

blocks.note: six letters running straight on across the gaps between the three words

annotation.surface: Joining in with a bout of public groping, and how badly the old are treated.
annotation.walkthrough: Terribly sits exactly where an anagram indicator would sit and shuffles nothing, because the letters are already standing in the order they are wanted. Frottage is rubbing up against strangers for gratification, the Eye supplying its own smut.
annotation.definitionFit: An ageist treats the old as lesser purely on account of their years, which is the prejudice behind being unkind to the elderly.

entries.clue: Awful grief at the end for Epstein emailer (6)

indicatorNotes.Awful: Something awful has gone badly wrong, and letters that have gone wrong are not left standing in their printed order.

blocks.note: five of the six letters the anagram works on
the letter that the little word the finishes on

annotation.surface: Dreadful sorrow arriving right at the finish.
annotation.walkthrough: The end that matters is the end of the word the rather than the end of anything in the picture, and it yields one letter. The email in question called Epstein a supreme friend and was published in 2025.
annotation.definitionFit: Fergie is what every British paper calls Sarah Ferguson, the Duchess of York, whose grovelling emails to Epstein surfaced in 2025.

entries.clue: What Trump likes to do – lead badly! (4)

indicatorNotes.badly: What is done badly comes out wrong, and letters that come out wrong come out in the wrong order.

blocks.note: the four letters the anagram works on

annotation.surface: Trump's favourite activity, and a verdict on his leadership.
annotation.walkthrough: Lead means leadership in the sentence and is four letters to reorder in the parse. The Eye's dig is that the man who put his name to The Art of the Deal leads badly.
annotation.definitionFit: Trump sells himself as a dealmaker, so what he likes to do is deal — the verb, in its bargaining sense.

entries.clue: Andrew no longer entertains love – very diminished sphere of activity (8)

indicatorNotes.entertains: To entertain a guest is to have them inside the house, so what follows goes within the word before it.

love is the tennis scorer's nothing, written as a nought
v is the standard short form of very

annotation.surface: Andrew, stripped of his titles, with a great deal less left to occupy him.
annotation.walkthrough: Andrew is not the wordplay's subject but its casualty: what he is no longer is what supplies the outer letters, and the removal of the title was real news in 2025. Love is the tennis zero.
annotation.definitionFit: A province is the field a person's authority covers, as in that is not my province, so it names a sphere of activity rather than a territory.

entries.clue: Brown's unfinished plan (4)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: A word left unfinished stops short of the letter it would have ended on.

blocks.note: a chart is a plan of action set out on paper
the letter that word ends on, and the one never reached

annotation.surface: A scheme of Gordon Brown's that was never seen through.
annotation.walkthrough: Brown is capitalised only because the sentence starts there, and the Eye is happy for you to spend a while on the former prime minister. It is a verb, and the thing heat does to toast.
annotation.definitionFit: To char something is to scorch it until it darkens, which is what brown means of food given too much heat.

entries.clue: (& 27ac.) Trump's Middle East gamble and each emerging cock-up (6)

entries.clue: Accommodation right for hot stimulating (7)

indicatorNotes.right for hot: Right and hot are each a single letter in a crossword, and for puts the first of them where the second was standing.

blocks.note: housing is the word for accommodation, taken before anything happens to it

annotation.walkthrough: The clue names two single letters and never says what word they sit in, so the accommodation has to be found first. H is the hot tap and R the right turn; both are worth knowing on sight.

entries.clue: Mentions relocating a place of high profile ICE activity (9)

annotation.definition: place of high profile ICE activity

the ninth letter, the article taken as itself

annotation.walkthrough: The a belongs to the letters being moved, not to the definition it appears to introduce, and that is the single decision the clue turns on. ICE is the US immigration force whose raids dominated the news.

entries.clue: Look into Archer novel filled with half lies (8)

indicatorNotes.novel: Novel means new, and letters made new are not the ones you were given standing in the order you were given them.
indicatorNotes.filled with: What a thing is filled with has gone inside it, so those letters sit within the others.

the back two letters of that word

annotation.surface: Jeffrey Archer's latest book padded out with half-truths.
annotation.walkthrough: Archer is the novelist who went to prison for perjury, which is what makes the half lies funny. Novel is not describing his book at all but telling you to reorder his name.
annotation.definitionFit: To research a subject is to look into it methodically, the verb standing in for the verb with nothing lost.

entries.clue: One advised to take "a different line in court"? (6)

annotation.definitionFit: A client is the person a solicitor or barrister acts for, named here by the service being bought rather than by the fee.

entries.clue: Sex act, flop – exploited by UK far right? (5,4)

annotation.definitionNote: The clue never names the thing, pointing at it instead by who has been waving it lately, so the definition is a description of the answer's recent use rather than a noun that could replace it.

to flag is to droop and lose all energy, the same sagging as a flop

annotation.surface: Sex that turned out to be a complete washout.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition names no flag at all: it points at the Raise the Colours campaign that ran banners up lampposts across England through 2025. Flop and flag meet in the sense of drooping rather than of failing.
annotation.definitionFit: The Union Flag is Britain's national flag, and it is the one the far right has claimed as its own, so the clue identifies it by the people flying it.

entries.clue: Boyfriend for example getting out of a shag? (5)

eg is the short form of exempli gratia, and it is the pair that departs

annotation.surface: A boyfriend, say, climbing out of bed after sex.
annotation.walkthrough: Getting out of a shag reads as leaving the bed, and the letters leaving are the abbreviation for example rather than an instance of one. What is left of the slang is the romance without the act.
annotation.definitionFit: A lover is the person someone is having the affair with, which boyfriend names in a steadier and more respectable register.

entries.clue: (& 12ac./24dn.) Dumbo occupying the chamber, an embarrassment to be ignored? (8)

the word taken straight off the page, letter for letter

annotation.walkthrough: Occupying sits exactly where a container instruction belongs and is really just the word in, spelt out. Four ordinary words in a row is a rare shape for a clue this long, which is why it reads as a sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: The elephant in the room is the huge obvious problem everyone present has agreed to say nothing about, which is the embarrassment the clue leaves ignored.

entries.clue: Our scrutiny of the press is cut – with a time check (9)

entries.clue: Let's go reckless with Trump's lead? Piss off! (3,4)

entries.clue: An idle sort of refusal to accept the vote? (6)
